A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same APM research and contain 30 pages, including Appendices A–H. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. The localized Figure 13 layout problem in v3 does not prevent assessment.

before.justification: v2 reports original computational evaluations of protein folding, inverse folding, complex generation, antibody design, peptide design, and longer binder design, with additional analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original computational results and reports revised binder evaluations, including the added TNF-α target in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The Seq&BB, Sidechain, and Refine modules, protein representation, training objectives, two-phase training, and sampling procedures remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A, B, and D.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds binder design against the TNF-α trimer, represented by 1tnf, to the six existing biological targets. Three existing targets use different PDB structures, but they are not three additional target types. Other training and evaluation coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 11 retains RFDiffusion and the APM variant with ProteinMPNN sequence redesign alongside APM. This same comparison set is used for TNF-α. Comparator membership in the other experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix F replaces the target/reference complexes 3di3 with 7opb, 6m0j with 7zsd, and 4z18 with 8znl. The added TNF-α experiment specifies a 50-residue binder. The top-eight folding selection, absence of hotspot specification, and success thresholds of pLDDT > 80 and ipTM > 0.8 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 13 revises the structural case studies comparing generated binders with their highest-pLDDT refoldings: three target-complex examples are replaced and TNF-α is added. The existing all-atom ablation, chain-by-chain analyses, torsion distributions, and antibody/peptide error cases remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix D.2 retains the same 20-random-seed folding comparison, mean±standard-deviation reporting, and significance statements in Table 7. The binder update introduces no new uncertainty estimates or changed repeated-run reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 11 replaces results for three PDB inputs and adds TNF-α results. For example, APM's ΔG of -80.10 on 3di3 is replaced by -55.72 on 7opb, which is not a same-setting performance change. On TNF-α, APM and RFDiffusion report ΔG values of -48.99 and -74.35; all three evaluated methods have 0% success. Tables 1–10 and the retained Table 11 cases are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, flow-matching derivations, losses, and sampling equations remain unchanged, including Equations 1–26. Changes from 'Appendix' to 'Section' in cross-references do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and concluding discussion retain the same claims about native multi-chain modeling, all-atom generation, folding/inverse-folding capabilities, and downstream antibody and peptide design.

C2.justification: Appendix F changes the statement that APM is comparable to RFDiffusion by explicitly excepting the TNF-α trimer target. The existing interpretations of low confidence scores, need for wet-lab validation, and broader limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F updates the PDB identifiers documenting evaluation inputs and specifies the TNF-α binder length as 50 residues because no bound reference structure was found. Architecture sizes, training hardware and budgets, other implementation details, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, main related-work section, and extended related work in Appendix E are unchanged. The binder revision adds no citations or new positioning against prior research.

P1.justification: v3 standardizes author-affiliation markers, changes appendix cross-reference wording to 'Section,' and makes localized edits to Appendix F. The overall narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 11 expands from six to seven target groups, and Figure 13 replaces three example rows and adds TNF-α. Nearby appendix text reflows. Figure 13's caption still incorrectly says 'six' targets and now overlaps the page-number area; other figures and tables retain their displays.

improvement.justification: The added TNF-α evaluation exposes difficulty on a trimeric binder target, and Appendix F explicitly qualifies the comparison with RFDiffusion. This modestly improves evidence about applicability beyond v2's six-target evaluation. The gain is limited by unexplained substitutions of three PDB inputs and Figure 13's caption/layout defects; the central method and main experimental evidence remain unchanged.
